messages.subject: Bivariate normality underlying polychoric correlations
parts:
Dear Lavaan-Team,

I recently read the LISREL-manual from Karl G. Jöreskog. He describes there on page 18 http://www.ssicentral.com/lisrel/techdocs/ordinal.pdf how to evaluate the bivariate normality of the data with a RMSEA measure.

"I have developed an RMSEA measure of population discrepancy similar to Steiger's (1990) RMSEA measure for structural equation models. The theory for this is outlined in Appendix 1. By further simulation studies based on varying degree of underlying bivariate non-normality I have found that there are no serious effects of non-normality unless RMSEA is larger than 0.1"

Is there a possibility to do something like this with lavaan or semTools? Maybe I have missed something obvious in the documentation.

I would be very thankful for any help!

Best regards

Pete

This is now implemented in the dev version (0.5-15). Although I
currently rely on the model-implied model statistics (I need a switch to
change that).

efficacy <- read.table("EFFICACY.IMP")
names(efficacy) <- c("NOSAY","VOTING","COMPLEX","NOCARE","TOUCH","INTEREST")

# all ordered
efficacy[,] <- lapply(efficacy, ordered)

# one-factor
model <- ' f =~ NOSAY + VOTING + COMPLEX + NOCARE + TOUCH + INTEREST'
fit <- cfa(model, data=efficacy, estimator="WLS")

# note: LR is based on model-implied statistics, not SAMPSTAT statistics!!!
lavTablesFit(fit)
lavTablesFit(fit, stat="RMSEA", p.value=TRUE)


I do struggle with the formulas given in Appendix 1 of the document
mentioned above. If I apply the formula using the numbers from the table
on page 17, I get (for the first row):

> sqrt( (222.381 - 8)/(2*1589*8) )
[1] 0.09182717

If I omit the '2', I get

> sqrt( (222.381 - 8)/(1589*8) )
[1] 0.1298632

which seems to correspond much closer to the 0.130 reported in the RMSEA
column on page 17.

Is this is a bug in prelis? Or did I misread the formulas?



Yves.

parts:
On 09/13/2013 12:31 PM, Pete Parkers wrote:

> > Warning in pchisq(out$str.sum, ncp = 0.1^2 * out$nobs * out$df,
> df = out$df, :
> > full precision may not have been achieved in 'pnchisq'

From ?pchisq:

The non-central ï¿½pchisqï¿½ is for ï¿½ncp < 80ï¿½ computed from the
Poisson mixture of central chi-squares and for larger ï¿½ncpï¿½ _via_
a C translation of

Ding, C. G. (1992) Algorithm AS275: Computing the non-central
chi-squared distribution function. _Appl.Statist._, *41* 478-482.

which computes the lower tail only (so the upper tail suffers from
cancellation and a warning will be given when this is likely to be
significant).

So instead of using lower.tail=FALSE, I had to use 1 - pchisq( ... ,
lower.tail=TRUE) and the warning(s) went away.

Fixed in dev 0.5-15.

Yves.

But (as I mentioned in the beginning of this thread) the lavTablesFit()
function uses the 'model-implied' (or 'restricted') cell proportions,
while prelis uses the sample-based or 'unrestricted' cell proportions
(simply based on the thresholds and polychoric correlations).

head( lavTablesFit(efaUnrotate.A_nf2, stat="LR") )
lhs rhs df LR
1 a1 a2 15 89.736
2 a1 a3 15 30.615
3 a1 a4 15 148.645
4 a1 a5 15 127.764
5 a1 a6 15 54.394
6 a1 a7 15 64.722

The LR values are not the same, and therefore the RMSEA values can not
be the same (even if you omit the 2 factor).

The lavTable* functions are very much under development, and one version
will mimic the prelis output.

Stay tuned.

Yves.

It turns out the discrepancies are due to the way lavaan handles empty
cells in bivariate tables. In 0.5-14, 0.5 is added to all empty cells.
In the currenct dev version (0.5-15), 0.5 is added only for 2x2 tables.
Nothing is added for larger tables.

The output of lavTables() is now (up to 2 digits after the decimal
point) identical to the PRELIS output for your data.

> A <- read.csv("A.csv")
> A[,] <- lapply(A[,], ordered)
> head( lavTables(A, type="table", stat=c("LR.BVN", "RMSEA.BVN"),
p.value=TRUE) )

lhs rhs nobs df LR.BVN LR.BVN.pval RMSEA.BVN RMSEA.BVN.pval
1 a1 a2 830 15 57.461 0.000 0.058 1
2 a1 a3 830 15 29.753 0.013 0.034 1
3 a1 a4 830 15 53.133 0.000 0.055 1
4 a1 a5 830 15 43.185 0.000 0.048 1
5 a1 a6 830 15 38.096 0.001 0.043 1
6 a1 a7 830 15 41.426 0.000 0.046 1
